title: Isofibrations induce Kan fibrations on cores
statement:
Use quasicategories, equivalence edges, cores and Kan complexes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a quasicategory $\mathcal C$, its core $\mathcal C^\simeq$ is the simplicial subset consisting of those simplices every edge of which is an equivalence. An isofibration $p:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ between quasicategories means a map lifting every inner horn and every equivalence edge $p(c)\to d$ to an equivalence edge with source $c$. A Kan fibration means a simplicial map lifting all horns $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$. For every isofibration $p$, the induced map
$$p^\simeq:\mathcal C^\simeq\longrightarrow\mathcal D^\simeq$$
is a Kan fibration. For every Kan complex $K$, every edge of $K$ is an equivalence and $K^\simeq=K$ as simplicial subsets.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.3.7 (Kerodon Tag 01EZ) for the map of cores; Proposition 4.4.2.1 (Kerodon Tag 019D), equivalence of (b) and (d), for a Kan complex having every edge invertible. Read both statements and proofs online on 2026-10-17. These are Kerodon tags, not the unrelated Stacks tags. WANTED: archived source.

proof.text: Work in a common universe containing the simplicial sets $C$ and $D$. First $p$ carries equivalence edges to equivalence edges: apply the simplicial map $p$ to an inverse edge and its two witnessing $2$-simplices in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Thus it sends every simplex whose edges are equivalences into the corresponding core simplex and defines the asserted simplicial map $p^\simeq$. Fix a lifting problem $a:\Lambda_i^n\to C^\simeq$, $b:\Delta^n\to D^\simeq$ with $p^\simeq a=b|_{\Lambda_i^n}$. Compose with the core inclusions. Every edge already prescribed by $a$ is an equivalence in $C$, and every edge of $b$ is an equivalence in $D$. Two-out-of-three $(\ast)$: in a quasicategory $Q$, an edge $f:x\to y$ is an equivalence if and only if $[f]$ is an isomorphism of $hQ$ as in [lem-coef-homotopy-category-triangle-calculus]. If $g$ is an inverse, with $2$-simplices whose edges on $[0,1],[1,2],[0,2]$ are $(f,g,s_0x)$ and $(g,f,s_0y)$, that node gives $[g][f]=[s_0x]=1_x$ and $[f][g]=[s_0y]=1_y$. Conversely, if $[f]$ has an inverse, it is $[g]$ for an edge $g:y\to x$, since every morphism of $hQ$ is represented by an edge; the equalities $[g][f]=[s_0x]$ and $[f][g]=[s_0y]$ then give, by the same node, $2$-simplices with edges $(f,g,s_0x)$ and $(g,f,s_0y)$, so $g$ is an inverse in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a $2$-simplex with edges $f=01$, $g=12$, $h=02$ the node gives $[g][f]=[h]$; if two of $[f],[g],[h]$ are isomorphisms in the category $hQ$, so is the third. Hence if two of $f,g,h$ are equivalence edges, so is the third.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.3.7, horn lifting setup and preservation of equivalence witnesses.

proof.text: For $n=1,i=0$, the horn $\Lambda_0^1$ is the vertex $\{0\}$ and the isofibration assumption lifts the equivalence $b$ from its prescribed source to an equivalence edge in $C$. For $n=1,i=1$, the horn $\Lambda_1^1$ is the vertex $\{1\}$, prescribing $c\in C$ and an equivalence $e:d\to p(c)$. Choose an inverse $w:p(c)\to d$ and the inverse triangle with edges $01=w$, $12=e$, $02=\operatorname{id}_{p(c)}$, as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The same two inverse triangles, with the roles of $e$ and $w$ exchanged, witness that $w$ is an equivalence. Lift $w$ from $c$ by the source-lifting assumption, obtaining an equivalence $v:c\to c^{\prime}$ with $p(v)=w$ and $p(c^{\prime})=d$. On $\Lambda_0^2$ prescribe $01=v$ and $02=\operatorname{id}_c$, over that triangle. Its initial edge $v$ is an equivalence, so [lem-cbc-inner-fibration-equivalence-outer-horn-lift] supplies a triangle with these edges, lying exactly over the chosen base triangle. Its edge $u=12:c^{\prime}\to c$ maps to $e$. By the two-out-of-three fact $(\ast)$ of Step 1, $u$ is an equivalence because $v$ and $\operatorname{id}_c$ are. The identity edge has itself as inverse, with constant inverse triangles. Thus both one-dimensional horns lift into the core.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.3.7, dimension-one horns; prescribed-target lifting is expanded by an explicit inverse triangle and relative 2-horn lift.

proof.text: Now assume $n\geq2$. If $0<i<n$, the inner-fibration assumption on $p$ fills the prescribed horn over the given simplex $b$. If $i=0$, the ordered edge $[0,1]$ is in $\Lambda_0^n$: for every $n\geq2$ it lies in the face opposite vertex $2$, which is included because $2\ne0$. Its image under $a$ is an equivalence in $C$. The initial-horn clause of [lem-cbc-inner-fibration-equivalence-outer-horn-lift] therefore fills this square over $b$. If $i=n$, the edge $[n-1,n]$ lies in the horn (the face opposite $0$ suffices), and is likewise an equivalence under $a$; use the final-horn clause of the same node. All these fillers extend the original horn exactly and have image exactly $b$; equivalence lifting for $p$ is not needed in these dimensions.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.3.7, inner horns and outer horns via Proposition 4.4.2.13 and its opposite dual.

proof.text: Check that each filler from Step 3 lies in $C^\simeq$. For $n\geq3$, each ordered nondegenerate edge $[r,s]$ of $\Delta^n$ lies in an included face: choose a vertex $j$ different from $r,s,i$, which is possible among the $n+1\geq4$ vertices, and use the face opposite $j$. Its image is therefore already prescribed by $a$ and is an equivalence. Degenerate edges are identities, with their constant inverse triangles. When $n=2$, the horn has exactly two of the three edges, and both are equivalences; the two-out-of-three fact $(\ast)$ of Step 1 applied to this particular filler makes the third an equivalence. The definition of the core in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] now puts the entire filler in $C^\simeq$.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.3.7, final paragraph: all edges are in the horn for n>2; two-out-of-three in n=2.

proof.text: Steps 2-4 solve every square against $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$. This is precisely the Kan-fibration lifting property specified in the item. There is no lifting condition in dimension zero and no assertion that either core is nonempty.

source.place: Definition of Kan fibration; conclusion of Proposition 4.4.3.7.

proof.text: Finally let $K$ be a Kan complex. It is a quasicategory because its all-horn fillers include the inner horns of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Fix any edge $u$ of $K$. For every $n\geq2$, any final horn whose final edge is $u$ has a filler by the Kan assumption. Thus $u$ satisfies the final-edge extension property in the converse clause of [lem-cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling], and is an equivalence. Every edge of every simplex of $K$ is therefore an equivalence; by the core definition every such simplex is in $K^\simeq$. The reverse inclusion is the defining subset inclusion, so $K^\simeq=K$ degree by degree, compatibly with all operators. The empty Kan complex is included, since the edge assertion is then vacuous.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.2.1, Kan implies every edge invertible, derived using the converse of Theorem 4.4.2.6.
